definition: Present or found everywhere, or very widely.
example: Contactless payment terminals are now ubiquitous in the city.
nuance: Ubiquitous is often used comparatively; it need not mean literally every place.
prompt: A device has become a familiar sight across nearly every workplace.
options: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in everyday life.
The ubiquitous manuscript survives in just one private collection.
The ubiquitous device was unusually expensive.
The ubiquitous manager cheated his staff out of their overtime pay.
reasons: This sentence demonstrates the meaning: present or found everywhere, or very widely.
A single rare instance is not widespread.
Price does not establish how widely something is found.
This confuses the word with iniquitous, which means wicked; dishonesty says nothing about how widespread something is.

practice.prompt: A hiker keeps spotting the same flower on every trail in a mountain valley.
options: By late spring, yellow wildflowers are ubiquitous along the valley's trails.
The ubiquitous orchid grows on one shaded cliff and nowhere else in the valley.
The ubiquitous guide could name every plant the hikers passed along the way.
The hikers reached a ubiquitous decision to rest beside the stream.
reasons: Flowers lining nearly every path are spread throughout the area, which is exactly the idea.
A plant confined to a single spot is rare, the reverse of turning up all over.
Knowing about everything is not the same as being found everywhere.
Full agreement among a group is unanimous; this word describes how widely something is spread.
